23 // The protocol has two phases with deliberately different trust levels.
24 // Pre-authentication: bounded length-prefixed JSON, device identity and nonces.
25 // Post-authentication: only authenticated encrypted Session records are parsed.
26 // The server never accepts a repository password or a repository master key.
27 // Transport keys come from device provisioning, not from the login password.
28 // All numbers below are resource ceilings, checked before reading allocations.
29 constexpr quint32 MaxFrame = 8 * 1024 * 1024;
30 constexpr qint64 MaxObject = 64 * 1024 * 1024;
31 constexpr int PasswordRounds = 120000;
32 // Wire layout (all multi-byte integers are big-endian):
33 // uint32 frameLength | frameLength bytes
34 // Before authentication the payload is a single UTF-8 JSON object.
35 // After authentication the payload is a versioned crypto::seal envelope.
36 // The decrypted payload starts with a 32-byte transcript digest.
37 // The next eight bytes are the sender's unsigned message sequence number.
38 // The remaining bytes are one UTF-8 JSON request or response object.
39 // Sequence zero is used for login in each direction, not for ClientHello.
40 // Client-to-server and server-to-client sequence spaces advance independently.
41 // The sequence value must match exactly; there is no reordering window.
42 // The envelope supplies nonce freshness, encryption and ciphertext authentication.
43 // The transcript and sequence supply channel binding and replay protection.
44 // A MAC-valid packet does not skip namespace or role authorization checks.
45 // Limits are applied at framing, JSON inventory and individual-object levels.
46 // These checks are complementary: a legal-sized frame can still be malformed.
